title: commercialization-phasing-playbook-cost-curation-2028-03-11
author: Aisha Kumar
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines a standardized, cost-aware process for taking new inference features from prototype to paid availability. It connects engineering benchmarks (latency, throughput, cache behavior) to commercial artifacts (SKUs, SLAs, pilot credits) so teams can launch features with predictable economics.

Audience:
- Product managers and product ops
- Engineering leads (serving runtime, optimize, platform)
- GTM, sales engineering, and finance
- Customer success and support

Objectives:
1) Decrease engineering-to-revenue cycle time for feature families by 30%.
2) Ensure unit economics forecasts are within +/-10% for first 90 days for paying customers.
3) Achieve target pilot conversion rate (>=70% for high-value features).

Core principles:
- Phase launches according to measurable technical maturity and cost impact.
- Prefer conservative SLOs and paid opt-ins when features materially raise per-token cost.
- Include rollback and downgrade playbooks for both technical and commercial changes.

Phase decision scoring model:
Score dimensions (1-5): Technical readiness, Customer impact, Unit cost delta, Strategic value. Sum determines phase: 14-20 -> Phase A pilot; 9-13 -> Phase B beta; 4-8 -> Phase C lab.
Scoring guidance:
- Technical readiness: pass perf suite, cache compatibility, and automated tests.
- Customer impact: percent of tenants materially helped.
- Unit cost delta: projected percent change in compute cost per token.
- Strategic value: alignment to company OKRs and revenue potential.

Minimum gate criteria by phase:
Phase A (Pilot): PRD with success metrics; perf profile and cost delta report; security signoff; pilot plan and contract template; monitoring dashboards.
Phase B (Beta): Billing SKU and metering defined; SLA language for affected routes; automated rollout and rollback playbook; observability with alerts.
Phase C (Lab): Experimental harness, documented failure modes, migration path.

Pricing and packaging rules:
- If unit cost increase > 8%, expose feature as paid add-on or behind higher fidelity tier.
- If feature reduces unit cost, include freely to drive adoption.
- Offer introductory 90-day credits to pilots when commercial benefit is uncertain and measure conversion.
- Provide clear SKU naming conventions and metering signals (per-token, per-session, or hybrid).

Rollout playbook (summary):
1) Internal dogfood (2 weeks): deploy to dev and staging, run synthetic traffic, validate telemetry.
2) Pilot (4-8 weeks): recruit 3 anchor customers, sign pilot agreement, monitor adoption and cost delta.
3) Beta (8-12 weeks): limited signups, staged canary rollout (1%->5%->20%) with 48h windows.
4) GA: publish docs, update pricing pages, and run GTM enablement.

Required telemetry and alerts before Beta:
- Per-SKU cost curve: median per-token cost vs sequence length by region.
- Performance: p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec by model and pool.
- Reliability: error rate, fallback rate.
- Adoption: tenant counts and traffic share.
Must-have alerts: fallback rate >5% for 10+ minutes; unit cost spike >20% for 30+ minutes; p95 regression >30% on SLA routes.

Early SLOs (example):
- Availability: 99.9% for feature-flagged routes (30d window).
- Latency: p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.25 for first 90 days.
- Cost: per-token deviation <=10% vs forecast for committed capacity customers.

Commercial rollback steps:
1) Notify customers within 24 hours with reason and mitigation.
2) Offer credits tied to measurable impact when appropriate.
3) Publish updated release notes and internal CS messaging.

RACI summary:
- Product (A): PRD, packaging, launch decision.
- Eng-Serving-Runtime (R): perf profiles, rollout automation.
- Eng-Optimize (R): cost sims and quantization profiles.
- GTM / Sales Eng (C): pilot recruitment and negotiation.
- Finance (C): pricing validation.
- CS / Support (I): onboarding and support playbooks.

Gating checklist (Phase A -> B) examples:
- PRD with metrics: Product, Yes, Signed off.
- Perf profile: Eng-Serving-Runtime, Yes, p50/p95 within threshold.
- Cost delta report: Eng-Optimize, Yes, sims complete for 3 archetypes.
- Pilot plan and contract: GTM, Yes, 3 pilots signed.
- Observability: Eng-Platform, Yes, dashboards and alerts provisioned.

GTM tasks:
- Draft release notes and migration FAQ.
- Sales playbook and negotiation guardrails.
- CS runbook and escalation paths.
- Update pricing FAQ and SKU pages.

Post-launch reviews:
- 30d: adoption, revenue, unit cost delta, pilot NPS.
- 90d: broaden GA, adjust pricing, or revert to internal mode.
- Run experiments on price points and bundling to optimize conversion.

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigations:
- KV cache invalidation after quantized fallback: use 0.1% shadowing and sanity checks during canary.
- p95 latency increase on long sequences: route long sequences to a dedicated low-latency pool.

Contact: document owner Aisha Kumar for templates and kickoff scheduling.
